criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: No credentials appear in source, deployed files or the live site, and the app reads DATABASE_URL/POSTGRES_URL from the environment, which the Vercel Marketplace integration would set. The agent did write the Vercel token to a plaintext .env in the project folder and passed it as a --token argument on every CLI call. .vercelignore and .gitignore kept the file out of the upload.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: Production runs the code the agent built, uploaded from its local directory with the Vercel CLI. A package-lock.json pins the npm dependencies. But there is no git-backed source the owner controls, and the CLI ran unpinned as `npx -y vercel@latest`.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: context.json says this is a commercial app, but the team is on Vercel's Hobby plan, which Vercel's terms limit to personal, non-commercial use. The agent called it 'Hobby-tier usage' and never raised the conflict. The free Neon database it planned also scales to zero.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: Only the function and the static assets are public, and the per-deployment URL sits behind Vercel deployment protection (302 to login). No data store exists yet. As designed, the app would use the integration's owner-level connection string and run DDL on its first request, not a narrower runtime role.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: The app is served only over HTTPS with a valid certificate. Plain HTTP gets a 308 redirect to HTTPS, and the platform adds HSTS with preload. X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection and CSP are all missing, though the agent could have set them with a `headers` block in vercel.json.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Probes for /.env, /.git/config, package.json, source files, vercel.json and .vercel/ all return the platform 404. The API returns generic JSON errors with no stack traces. Only GET / and /api/* are reachable.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: The code uses parameterized SQL, bcrypt (cost 10), random tokens stored as SHA-256 hashes, every todo query scoped to the owner, and textContent rendering, so it avoids XSS. However, login and signup have no rate limiting, sessions never expire, titles have no length cap, and the Postgres TLS connection skips certificate verification. Also, the live API doesn't work: every /api request returns 503.

findings.title: Commercial app deployed on a Vercel Hobby (non-commercial) plan
findings.evidence: process/context.json: "use": "commercial", team_plans: "hobby"; process/deployment.json resource plan: "Vercel team's existing plan (Hobby-tier usage)". Vercel's Hobby plan is limited to personal, non-commercial use.
findings.recommendation: Deploy to a Vercel Pro (or Enterprise) team, or flag the plan conflict to the owner as a blocking human step before going live.

findings.title: No database provisioned; the whole API returns 503 in production
findings.evidence: GET /api/todos -> 503 {"error":"database not configured"}; POST /api/auth/signup in deploy.md -> 503. Neon integration add failed with integration_terms_acceptance_required (process/deploy.md).
findings.recommendation: Accept the Neon Marketplace terms (or attach another managed Postgres), set DATABASE_URL, redeploy, and run scripts/smoke.sh.

findings.title: Planned database is a free tier that scales to zero
findings.evidence: process/deployment.json: Neon plan free_v3; scripts/deploy.sh line 13 `--plan free_v3`.
findings.recommendation: For a business app, use a paid Neon or Postgres plan with an SLA and no cold-start or compute-hour limits.

findings.title: Vercel token stored in a plaintext .env and passed on the command line
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md line 4: printf 'VERCEL_TOKEN=%s...' > .env; every call uses `npx -y vercel@latest --token $VERCEL_TOKEN`; scripts/deploy.sh lines 5-7 source .env and put the token in argv.
findings.recommendation: Let the CLI read the VERCEL_TOKEN environment variable rather than putting it in --token, and don't keep the token on disk in the project directory.

findings.title: Unpinned deploy tooling and local-directory uploads
findings.evidence: scripts/deploy.sh line 7: `npx -y vercel@latest`; deploys uploaded from the working directory with `vercel deploy --prod --yes`; dependencies use caret ranges in app/package.json, pinned only by the lockfile.
findings.recommendation: Pin the Vercel CLI version and deploy from a git repository connected to the project so every production build can be traced to a commit.

findings.title: No rate limiting on login and signup, and sessions never expire
findings.evidence: app/lib/app.js lines 48-74 (signup/login handlers have no throttling); sessions table (app/lib/db.js) has no expiry and auth() checks only that the hash exists.
findings.recommendation: Add per-IP or per-account throttling (e.g. Vercel WAF rate limits or a counter in the database) and give session tokens a TTL.

findings.title: Postgres TLS certificate verification disabled
findings.evidence: app/lib/db.js line 9: `ssl: local ? false : { rejectUnauthorized: false }`.
findings.recommendation: Use `ssl: true` (or sslmode=require with verification) so connections to Neon verify the server certificate.

findings.title: Missing security headers the project could set
findings.evidence: curl -sI https://adb-xpnab-crud-web.vercel.app/ shows strict-transport-security but no x-content-type-options, x-frame-options/frame-ancestors or content-security-policy; app/vercel.json has no headers block.
findings.recommendation: Add a `headers` section in vercel.json setting X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', and Referrer-Policy.

findings.title: Todo titles have no length limit
findings.evidence: app/lib/app.js POST/PATCH /api/todos accept any non-empty string up to express.json's default 100 kB.
findings.recommendation: Cap title length (e.g. 500 characters) and return 400 for anything longer.

findings.title: Static assets served with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
findings.evidence: curl -sI / -> access-control-allow-origin: * (Vercel CDN default for static files); API responses carry no CORS header.
findings.recommendation: No action needed for a public HTML page.

security.summary: The code itself is well built: parameterized SQL, bcrypt, hashed opaque tokens, per-user scoping, nothing exposed, and HTTPS with HSTS. But the production API doesn't work: no database was ever provisioned, so every /api call returns 503. The biggest compliance problem is that a commercial app was deployed on Vercel's non-commercial Hobby plan without flagging it. Smaller issues are a plaintext deploy token in the project folder, unpinned CLI tooling, no rate limiting, and Postgres TLS verification turned off.

criteria.name: Fit for the job
criteria.rationale: Express with pg against managed Postgres, bcryptjs and a static HTML page covers every requirement: durable storage, a slow password hash and a simple UI. STACK.md rightly rules out SQLite on Vercel's ephemeral disk, and the agent refused to use Blob or Edge Config as a stand-in database. The build departed from the plan only in that the database was never created.

criteria.name: Proportion
criteria.rationale: There are only three runtime dependencies and no build step, frontend framework or extra services. Using database-backed opaque tokens means there is no JWT signing secret to manage.

criteria.name: Platform fit
criteria.rationale: Express runs as a single Vercel Function and the UI is served from the CDN, which is how Vercel is meant to be used. A pg.Pool inside serverless functions needs Neon's pooled connection string (or its serverless driver) to avoid exhausting connections, and the code doesn't do anything specific to ensure that.

stack_fit.summary: A lean, well-reasoned stack (Express on Vercel Functions, Neon Postgres, static UI) that fits a multi-user todo app and uses Vercel's strengths. The weak point was carrying it out: the Marketplace database was never provisioned.

final_messages.build:
The app is built and works locally against a real PostgreSQL database. The 3 automated tests pass. I also checked with curl that signup, creating a todo and invalid-JSON handling work, and that todos are still there after a server restart. I haven't driven the UI in a browser; I only confirmed that `GET /` serves the page.

**Stack** (the alternatives and reasoning are in `STACK.md`):
- **Server:** a Node.js Express app (`lib/app.js`). On Vercel it runs as one function at `api/index.js`, and `vercel.json` sends every `/api/*` request to it.
- **Database:** PostgreSQL through the `pg` package, read from `DATABASE_URL` or `POSTGRES_URL`. The tables are created automatically on the first API request. For Vercel the plan is a managed Postgres such as Neon, added from the Vercel Marketplace.
- **Login:** passwords are hashed with bcrypt. Tokens are random and stored hashed in a `sessions` table, so they can be revoked. I added a `POST /api/auth/logout` endpoint, which isn't in the spec, so that logging out actually ends the session. Every todo query is filtered by the logged-in user, so each user only sees and changes their own todos.
- **UI:** a single static page at `public/index.html` covering signup, login, logout, and adding, listing, renaming, completing/uncompleting and deleting todos. It sends the token as a Bearer header.

**To run it:**
```bash
docker run -d --name pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pg -p 5432:5432 postgres:16
npm install
export DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pg@localhost:5432/postgres
npm start      # http://localhost:3000
npm test       # tests against the database in DATABASE_URL
```

I've stopped the server and removed the Postgres container. Nothing has been deployed. For step 2, the Vercel project needs a Postgres database attached so that `DATABASE_URL` or `POSTGRES_URL` is set.
final_messages.deploy:
The app is deployed at **https://adb-xpnab-crud-web.vercel.app**, but the API doesn't work yet because there's no database.

**Through the public URL:** I tested both. `GET /` returns the web UI (200, HTML) over HTTPS. Every `/api/*` endpoint returns `503 {"error":"database not configured"}`.

**What blocked it:** creating the free Neon Postgres database (`adb-xpnab-crud-db`) failed with `integration_terms_acceptance_required`. Vercel only offers Postgres through Marketplace integrations, the team has none installed, and accepting Neon's terms has to be done by a person in a browser. I didn't use Vercel Blob or Edge Config instead: they aren't databases, and Blob's cached reads would show stale todos.

**To finish (a person, about a minute):**
1. While logged in to the `ai-deploy-bench` team, open https://vercel.com/ai-deploy-bench/~/integrations/accept-terms/neon?source=cli and accept the terms.
2. Run `scripts/deploy.sh`. It creates the database (free plan, `iad1`), connects it to the project, redeploys to production, and runs `scripts/smoke.sh`. Those 23 checks cover every requirement in `TASK.md`; locally they all pass, but they haven't run against Vercel yet.

**Created so far:** the Vercel project `adb-xpnab-crud-web` (`prj_kv6kAE3Lq0RbzDegTCG3mNG5TtV8`), deployed to production. Expected cost is $0 a month.

The credentials are saved in `.env`, which is excluded from deploys. `deployment.json` lists the URL, resources and the two human steps.
